narrative.title: Best Window in a Power Trading Ledger
narrative.scenario: A grid trader logs the net megawatt balance for each interval of the day, where selling shows as positive and drawing power shows as negative. The desk wants the most profitable contiguous block of intervals. A block must be non-empty, so a day of only losses must report the least painful single interval rather than zero.
narrative.inputFormat: An array nums of n integers, one net balance per interval.
narrative.outputFormat: The largest possible sum of a non-empty contiguous subarray of nums.

testCases.explanation: The block 4,-1,2,1 totals 6, and including either neighbouring negative would drag it down.
A single interval is the only legal block, so its value is the answer.

hintLevels: Level 1: Ask what the best block ending exactly at the current interval is - that answer only depends on the previous interval.
Level 2: Extend the running total with the current balance and update a global best from it; whenever the running total turns negative, drop it because a fresh block always beats carrying that debt.
Level 3: The best value must start below every possible balance, and dropping the running total to zero is only safe if you never let that zero become the recorded answer on an all-negative day.
